source.title: Civics (History and Government) Questions for the Naturalization Test (2008 test, rev. 01/19)

review.note: Wording and answers were machine-extracted from the official PDF and validated for counts and structure. No qualified human or legal review has been performed yet.

questions.prompt: What is the supreme law of the land?
What does the Constitution do?
The idea of self-government is in the first three words of the Constitution. What are these words?
What is an amendment?
What do we call the first ten amendments to the Constitution?
What is one right or freedom from the First Amendment?
How many amendments does the Constitution have?
What did the Declaration of Independence do?

answers.text: said that the United States is free (from Great Britain)

questions.prompt: What are two rights in the Declaration of Independence?
What is freedom of religion?

answers.text: You can practice any religion, or not practice a religion.

questions.prompt: What is the economic system in the United States?
What is the “rule of law”?

answers.text: No one is above the law.

questions.prompt: Name one branch or part of the government.
What stops one branch of government from becoming too powerful?
Who is in charge of the executive branch?
Who makes federal laws?
What are the two parts of the U.S. Congress?
How many U.S. Senators are there?
We elect a U.S. Senator for how many years?
Who is one of your state’s U.S. Senators now?

answers.note: District of Columbia residents and residents of U.S. territories should answer that D.C. (or the territory where the applicant lives) has no U.S. Senators.

dynamic.lookupLabel: Find your state's senators on senate.gov

questions.prompt: The House of Representatives has how many voting members?
We elect a U.S. Representative for how many years?
Name your U.S. Representative.

answers.note: Residents of territories with nonvoting Delegates or Resident Commissioners may provide the name of that Delegate or Commissioner. Also acceptable is any statement that the territory has no (voting) Representatives in Congress.

dynamic.lookupLabel: Find your representative on house.gov (a ZIP code can span districts; confirm your address)

If both the President and the Vice President can no longer serve, who becomes President?
Who is the Commander in Chief of the military?

Who vetoes bills?

answers.text: Secretary of Health and Human Services
Secretary of Housing and Urban Development

questions.prompt: What does the judicial branch do?

answers.text: decides if a law goes against the Constitution

questions.prompt: Under our Constitution, some powers belong to the federal government. What is one power of the federal government?
Under our Constitution, some powers belong to the states. What is one power of the states?
Who is the Governor of your state now?

answers.note: District of Columbia residents should answer that D.C. does not have a Governor.

questions.prompt: What is the capital of your state?

answers.note: District of Columbia residents should answer that D.C. is not a state and does not have a capital. Residents of U.S. territories should name the capital of the territory.

dynamic.lookupLabel: Find your state government site on usa.gov

questions.prompt: What is the name of the Speaker of the House of Representatives now?

answers.text: Visit uscis.gov/citizenship/testupdates for the name of the Speaker of the House of Representatives.

questions.prompt: There are four amendments to the Constitution about who can vote. Describe one of them.

answers.text: You don’t have to pay (a poll tax) to vote.
Any citizen can vote. (Women and men can vote.)
A male citizen of any race (can vote).

questions.prompt: What is one responsibility that is only for United States citizens?
Name one right only for United States citizens.
What are two rights of everyone living in the United States?
What do we show loyalty to when we say the Pledge of Allegiance?
What is one promise you make when you become a United States citizen?

answers.text: give up loyalty to other countries
defend the Constitution and laws of the United States
obey the laws of the United States
serve in the U.S. military (if needed)
serve (do important work for) the nation (if needed)
be loyal to the United States

questions.prompt: How old do citizens have to be to vote for President?
What are two ways that Americans can participate in their democracy?

answers.text: give an elected official your opinion on an issue
publicly support or oppose an issue or policy

questions.prompt: When is the last day you can send in federal income tax forms?
When must all men register for the Selective Service?
What is one reason colonists came to America?
Who lived in America before the Europeans arrived?
What group of people was taken to America and sold as slaves?
Why did the colonists fight the British?

answers.text: because of high taxes (taxation without representation)
because the British army stayed in their houses (boarding, quartering)

questions.prompt: Who wrote the Declaration of Independence?
When was the Declaration of Independence adopted?

answers.text: The Founding Fathers wrote the Constitution.

questions.prompt: When was the Constitution written?

answers.text: oldest member of the Constitutional Convention
first Postmaster General of the United States
